name: Battle of Karbala
note: The accounts do not give the compass directions of the field, so the plan is drawn without them. The Euphrates is placed along the foot of the plan and the ditch behind Husayn's tents on the side away from the Kufans; the accounts do not say where either lay. The accounts do not say which units encircled Husayn's companions, nor what each flank was made of; the wings are placed by judgement. Husayn's companions are shown as two flanks, the tents and his relatives, as the accounts name them. Most accounts give thirty-two horsemen and forty infantrymen for Husayn and 4,000 for Ibn Sa'd; Shi'a sources say Ibn Sa'd's army had grown to 30,000.

phases.title: Both sides take up positions
phases.text: After the morning prayer both sides formed up. Husayn put Zuhayr ibn al-Qayn on his right and Habib ibn Muzahir on his left, with the tents tied together and the ditch behind them. The Kufan wings stood opposite, with 500 horsemen on the route to the river.
phases.quote: After the morning prayer on 10 October, both parties took up battle positions.

phases.title: Volleys of arrows and duels
phases.text: Zuhayr ibn al-Qayn tried to dissuade the Kufan soldiers from killing Husayn, but failed. The Kufans fired several volleys of arrows, and in the duels that followed several of Husayn's companions were slain.
phases.quote: Ibn Sa'd's army fired several volleys of arrows. This was followed by duels in which several of Husayn's companions were slain.

phases.title: The Kufan right wing attacks and is repulsed
phases.text: The right wing of the Kufans, under Amr ibn al-Hajjaj, attacked Husayn's force and was repulsed. Hand-to-hand fighting then paused and further volleys of arrows were exchanged.
phases.quote: The right wing of the Kufans, led by Amr ibn al-Hajjaj, attacked Husayn's force, but was repulsed.

phases.title: Shimr attacks and is repulsed
phases.text: Shimr, who commanded the left wing of the Umayyad army, launched an attack. There were losses on both sides, and he was repulsed.
phases.quote: Shimr, who commanded the left wing of the Umayyad army, launched an attack, but after losses on both sides he was repulsed.

phases.title: Cavalry attacks and Ibn Sa'd brings in reinforcements
phases.text: Cavalry attacks followed, and Husayn's cavalry resisted fiercely. Ibn Sa'd brought in armoured cavalry and five hundred archers.
phases.quote: Husayn's cavalry resisted fiercely and Ibn Sa'd brought in armoured cavalry and five hundred archers.

phases.title: The tents are burned and Husayn's companions are encircled
phases.text: Because the Kufans could approach only from the front, Ibn Sa'd ordered the tents burned, except the one Husayn and his family used. The flames hindered the Umayyad advance for a while. After noon prayers Husayn's companions were encircled.
phases.quote: Ibn Sa'd ordered all of the tents, except the one which Husayn and his family were using, to be burned.

phases.title: Husayn's relatives fight and Husayn is killed
phases.text: Husayn's relatives, who had not fought until then, joined the battle, and among those slain was his son Ali al-Akbar. Shimr advanced with foot soldiers, the Kufans rushed at Husayn, and he was killed.
phases.quote: The Kufan soldiers then rushed at Husayn and wounded him on his hand and shoulder.
